name: Yungay, Chile
use_case: The Atacama desert is one of the few places on Earth that combine hyperaridity, high solar UV flux, sedimentary plains, and soil chemistry similar to Mars’. It is amongst the most important benchmark sites when it comes to Mars research.
papers: The Atacama Rover Astrobiology Drilling Studies (ARADS) Project | 10.1089/ast.2022.0126

name: High Antartic Polar Plateau
use_case: The temperatures in the Antarctic offer the closest comparison to Mars’ ambient temperatures. The Antarctic, due to its isolated nature, is also an ideal site to test crew mentality when facing the isolation on Mars beforehand. This site is useful for testing subsurface life-detection instruments and habitat power and heating systems under extreme cold.
papers: ‘White Mars’ – nearly two decades of biomedical research at the Antarctic Concordia station | 10.1113/ep088352

name: Dallol, Danakil Depression
use_case: Dallol is an extremely hostile environment with multiple lethal conditions, making it interesting to test survivability and habitability. It also has the potential to become a site for biosignature identification equipment fine tuning to avoid false positive tests on Mars. This site could be useful for chemical-resistant equipment testing.
papers: The Dallol Geothermal Area, Northern Afar (Ethiopia)—An Exceptional Planetary Field Analog on Earth | 10.1089/ast.2018.1926

name: University Valley, Antartica
use_case: University Valley is a site permanently below freezing point and is home to dry permafrost. Its icy structures make it the ideal and most faithful analog site to Mars’ polar points, where extremely cold temperatures create similar conditions to the ones found in University Valley. The site is extremely useful for subsurface permafrost drill testing.
papers: X-RAY AMORPHOUS COMPONENTS OF ANTARCTICA DRY VALLEY SOILS: WEATHERING IMPLICATIONS FOR MARS | 20200001776 ; The high elevation Dry Valleys in Antarctica as analog sites for subsurface ice on Mars | 10.1016/j.pss.2013.05.019
notes: radius was calculated with numbers given in paper

name: Uhuru Peak, Mount Kilimanjaro
use_case: This high altitude, low atmospheric pressure, and high UV radiation site provides atmospheric conditions that are closest to Mars’. Composed of volcanic basalt and glacial ice, Mount Kilimanjaro proves to be an interesting research site when it comes to the movement of volcanic basalt on Mars. Microbial survival in this barren site could also be explored.
papers: The disappearing periglacial ecosystem atop Mt. Kilimanjaro supports both cosmopolitan and endemic microbial communities | 10.1038/s41598-019-46521-0

name: Kilauea Crater, Hawaii
use_case: The basaltic lava tubes in the subsurface of the Kilauea Crater make this site a close analog to the Martian shield volcanoes and basaltic plains. These lava tubes are studied to further understand Mars’ volcanology and subsurface structure. The Kilauea Crater is also used for subsurface cave exploration robotics.
papers: Terrestrial analogs to the calderas of the Tharsis volcanoes on Mars | 10.1017/cbo9780511536014.004 ; Basaltic Terrains in Idaho and Hawai‘i as Planetary Analogs for Mars Geology and Astrobiology | 10.1089/ast.2018.1847

name: Death Valley, California
use_case: Death Valley’s sand dunes and dried lakebeds rich in evaporites/sulfates make the site a very close analog to Mars’ ancient lakebeds and dusty surface. It is a useful site when analyzing how wind affects dust movement and erosion. Since the surface of Death Valley is extremely similar to Mars’, it is a favoured research site when it comes to testing rover mobility and other equipment.
papers: The Ibex dune field of Death Valley National Park, California: Characterization and assessment for Use as a Martian analog | 10.1016/j.aeolia.2026.101032
notes: there are two coords in the source, the one written is the first

name: Bodélé Depression, Chad
use_case: The dust and dried lakebeds in the Bodélé Depression make the site an interesting analog to Mars’ ancient lakebeds and dusty surfaces. The Bodélé Depression could be studied for wind and dust dynamics, erosion, and lakebed sediments. This site is the largest and most active source of atmospheric dust on Earth, replicating the intense atmospheric conditions on Mars.
papers: Links between topography, wind, deflation, lakes and dust: The case of the Bodélé Depression, Chad | 10.1029/2006GL025827
notes: the coords source presents many coordinates, so the final coordinate is an approx (+new site = no nasa coords)

name: Taklamakan Desert, Tarim basin
use_case: The Taklamakan Desert is an ideal research site when it comes to studying Martian dust and sediment behaviour. In fact, dust in the Taklamakan Desert is extremely small and has a longer suspension time, conditions that are by far the closest to the ones found on Mars. The site’s shifting sand dunes are also interesting to consider since their formations and shifts closely mimic the dynamics found on Mars. It is essential to test equipment in dusty environments.

name: Loma, Montana
use_case: Loma’s most appealing point is its daily temperature shift. Being the location with the largest temperature swing on Earth, it could be an interesting site for research on equipment behaviour outdoors when exposed to varying temperatures. It is essential to understand how equipment will expand and contract during the extreme daily temperature shifts on Mars.

name: Deccan Traps
use_case: The Deccan Traps are well-known for their basaltic grounds. As a primary analog site for Mars research, it allows studies on rock chemistry, their formation, and their potential extraction on Mars.
papers: Is continental flood basalt a potential analog for Martian crust? : A geochemical analysis | https://www.hou.usra.edu/meetings/lpsc2022/pdf/1067.pdf

name: Svalbard
use_case: Svalbard, Norway, is a well-known benchmark when it comes to studies on Mars analogs. Its basaltic grounds and cold climate make it an ideal site to test rover mobility and sample acquisition for the icy basaltic regolith on Mars.
papers: Polygon pattern geomorphometry on Svalbard (Norway) and western Utopia Planitia (Mars) using high-resolution stereo remote-sensing data | 10.1016/j.geomorph.2011.07.002
notes: the lat and long were obtained by doing a average of the latitude

name: Karoo Flood Basalt Province
use_case: As one of the largest flood basalt provinces, the Karoo Flood Basalt Province offers a potential site for research on flood basalt (the flow of lava over large surfaces), the oxidizing of iron-bearing minerals similar to the ones found on Mars, and subsurface magma movements.

name: Paraná Traps
use_case: The Paraná Traps is a rare site that combines impact cratering and basaltic grounds. As such, it is a valuable site for research on how impact cratering affects basalt areas, both of which are extremely present on Mars. Furthermore, subsurface hydrology (the presence of water in fractured basalt), could also be an interesting subject to study for future Mars explorations.
papers: The Paraná Magmatic Province: State-of-the-Art in the Geophysical and Geochemical Investigations | 10.22564/brjg.v40i6.2196 ; Volcanological aspects of the northwest region of Paraná continental flood basalts | 10.5194/se-6-227-2015

name: Chilcotin Group
use_case: The basaltic terrain and the volcanic plains make the Chilcotin Group a promising candidate in Mars analog research. Lava flow, mineralogy, and interactions between volcanic terrain and glacial processes could be studied to further understand the processes found on Mars.

use_case: Ladakh’s permafrost makes the site interesting for research on microbial survival and preservation under permanently freezing conditions. The site could be used to test life-detection equipment in ice-rich lake sediments.
